options.name: init_config
options.description: All options defined here are available to all instances.

options.name: use_instant_client
options.description:
Determines whether the Agent uses the Oracle Instant Client to connect instead of the Oracle native client. 
This option cannot be used at the same time as `jdbc_driver_path`.

options.name: propagate_agent_tags
options.description:
Set to `true` to propagate the tags from `datadog.yaml` and the agent host tags to the check.
When set to `true`, the tags from the agent host are added to the check's tags for all instances.

options.name: global_custom_queries
options.description:
See `custom_queries` defined below.

Global custom queries can be applied to all instances using the
`use_global_custom_queries` setting at the instance level.

options.name: service
options.description:
Attach the tag `service:<SERVICE>` to every metric, event, and service check emitted by this integration.

Additionally, this sets the default `service` for every log source.

options.name: instances
options.description: Every instance is scheduled independently of the others.

options.name: propagate_agent_tags
options.description:
Set to `true` to propagate the tags from `datadog.yaml` and the agent host tags to the check.

When set to `true`, the tags from the agent host are added to this instance's tags.
This option takes precedence over the `propagate_agent_tags` option in `init_config`.

options.name: server
options.description: The IP address or hostname of the Oracle Database Server.

options.name: service_name
options.description:
The Oracle Database service name. To view the services available on your server,
run the following query: `SELECT value FROM v$parameter WHERE name='service_names'`

options.name: protocol
options.description:
The protocol to connect to the Oracle Database Server. Valid protocols include TCP and TCPS.

If you are using the TCPS protocol and connecting to Oracle Database through JDBC, `jdbc_truststore` and
`jdbc_truststore_type` are required.

More information can be found from Oracle Database's whitepaper:
https://www.oracle.com/technetwork/topics/wp-oracle-jdbc-thin-ssl-130128.pdf

options.name: username
options.description: The username for the Datadog user account.

options.name: password
options.description: The password for the Datadog user account.

options.name: tns_alias
options.description:
The alias for the database connect string (stored in `tnsnames.ora` or in LDAP) to a CDB.
It's an alternative to specifying `server` and `service_name`. `tns_alias` requires
an Oracle software installation.

options.name: tns_admin
options.description:
The location of the Oracle client configuration files (`sqlnet.ora`, `tnsnames.ora`, `ldap.ora`).
This configuration is required only when using Oracle Instant Client. Oracle Instant Client
is required when `tns_alias` is set. Alternatively, you can set the environment variable
`TNS_ADMIN` before starting the Datadog Agent.

options.name: wallet
options.description: The directory containing the Oracle wallet. The Oracle wallet is used with the TCPS protocol.

options.name: oracle_client
options.description:
Force using an external Oracle client even when `tns_alias` isn't set. This might be necessary
for using some advanced Oracle SQLNet features which aren't supported by the
Oracle driver for Go. If you specify `tns_admin`, the Agent automatically tries
to use an external client. For Linux, if you are using Instant Client, set
the environment variable `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for the Agent process. If you are using
a client or server Oracle home, additionally set `ORACLE_HOME`.

options.name: query_timeout
options.description: The query timeout in seconds. Defaults to 20.

options.name: jdbc_driver_path
options.description:
Set this parameter if you are not using the Oracle native client or Instant Client.
You can also add it to your $CLASSPATH instead.

options.name: jdbc_truststore_path
options.description:
The JDBC truststore file path.

Note: This option is required if connecting with TCPS through JDBC.

options.name: jdbc_truststore_type
options.description:
The JDBC truststore file type. Supported truststore types include JKS, SSO, and PKCS12.

Note: This option is required if connecting with TCPS through JDBC.

options.name: jdbc_truststore_password
options.description: The password for the truststore when connecting through JDBC.

options.name: dbm
options.description: Set to `true` to enable Database Monitoring.

options.name: query_samples
options.description: Configure collection of query samples.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of query samples. Requires `dbm: true`.

options.name: include_all_sessions
options.description: Include all sessions in the query samples collection.

options.name: active_session_history
options.description:
Collect activity samples from `v$active_session_history` instead of the Agent performing sampling.

WARNING: Querying `v$active_session_history` requires optional Oracle licences and may result in
additional costs if enabled.

options.name: query_metrics
options.description: Configure collection of query metrics.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of query metrics. Requires enabled query samples.

options.name: collection_interval
options.description: The interval in seconds between query metrics collections.

options.name: db_rows_limit
options.description:
The maximum number of rows to fetch from each of the queries used to collect query metrics.
Query metrics are collected with two queries, so a single collection can fetch up to twice this value.

options.name: lookback
options.description: The lookback window in seconds used to select the query metrics to collect.

options.name: max_run_time
options.description:
The maximum time in seconds to spend collecting execution plans for a single query metrics collection.
This option only affects execution plan collection and has no effect when execution plans are disabled.

options.name: execution_plans
options.description: Configure collection of execution plans.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of execution plans. Requires query metrics.

options.name: plan_cache_retention
options.description: The number of minutes to retain execution plan metadata in the Agent cache.

options.name: sysmetrics
options.description: Configure collection of database sysmetrics.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of database sysmetrics.

options.name: tablespaces
options.description: Configure collection of tablespace usage.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of tablespace usage.

options.name: collection_interval
options.description: The interval in seconds between tablespace usage collections. Defaults to 600.

options.name: process_memory
options.description: Configure collection of process memory usage.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of process memory usage.

options.name: shared_memory
options.description: Configure collection of shared memory usage.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of database shared memory usages. Requires `dbm: true`.

options.name: inactive_sessions
options.description: Configure collection of inactive sessions.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of inactive sessions.

options.name: user_sessions_count
options.description: Configure collection of the user sessions count.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of the user sessions count.

options.name: asm
options.description: Configure collection of Automatic Storage Management (ASM) metrics. Requires `dbm: true`.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of Automatic Storage Management (ASM) metrics.

options.name: resource_manager
options.description: Configure collection of resource manager statistics. Requires `dbm: true`.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of resource manager statistics.

options.name: locks
options.description: Configure collection of locks metrics. Requires `dbm: true`.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable collection of locks metrics.

options.name: metric_collection_interval
options.description: The interval in seconds between metric collections. Defaults to 60.

options.name: database_instance_collection_interval
options.description: The interval in seconds between database instance metadata collections. Defaults to 300.

options.name: reported_hostname
options.description: Set the reported hostname for this instance. This value overrides the hostname detected by the Agent.

options.name: exclude_hostname
options.description: Omit the hostname from tags and events. This is useful when the database host is not monitored by an Agent.

options.name: database_identifier
options.description:
Controls how the database is identified. The default value is the resolved hostname for the instance,
which respects the `reported_hostname` option.

This value is used as-is for the display name of the instance but is normalized when applied as a tag.
Please see https://docs.datadoghq.com/getting_started/tagging/ for more details on Datadog tag normalization.

options.name: template
options.description:
The template to use for the database identifier. The default value is `$resolved_hostname`.
You can use the following variables, prefixed by `$` in the template:
- resolved_hostname: The resolved hostname of the instance, which respects the `reported_hostname` option.
- server: The provided server of the instance.
- port: The port number of the instance.
- service_name: The provided service name of the instance.
- cdb_name: The resolved CDB name of the instance.
In addition, you can use any key from the `tags` section of the configuration.

options.name: only_custom_queries
options.description:
Set this parameter to `true` if you want to skip the integration's default metrics collection.
Only metrics specified in `custom_queries` will be collected.

options.name: use_global_custom_queries
options.description:
How `global_custom_queries` should be used for this instance. There are 3 options:

1. true - `global_custom_queries` override `custom_queries`.
2. false - `custom_queries` override `global_custom_queries`.
3. extend - `global_custom_queries` are used in addition to any `custom_queries`.

options.name: custom_queries
options.description:
Each query must have 2 fields, and can have a third optional field:

1. query - The SQL to execute. It can be a simple statement or a multi-line script.
    Use the pipe `|` if you require a multi-line script.
2. columns - The list representing each column, ordered sequentially from left to right.
    The number of columns must equal the number of columns returned in the query.
    There are 2 required pieces of data:
      1. name - The suffix to append to `<INTEGRATION>.` to form
          the full metric name. If `type` is a `tag` type, this column is considered a tag and applied
          to every metric collected by this particular query.
      2. type - The submission method (gauge, monotonic_count, etc.).
          This can also be set to the following `tag` types to tag each metric in the row with the name
          and value of the item in this column:
            1. tag - This is the default tag type
            2. tag_list - This allows multiple values to be attached to the tag name. For example: 
                ```
                query = {
                  "name": "example",
                  "query": "...",
                  "columns": [
                    {"name": "server_tag", "type": "tag_list"},
                    {"name": "foo", "type": "gauge"},
                  ]
                }
                ```
                May result in:
                ```
                gauge("foo", tags=["server_tag:us", "server_tag:primary", "server_tag:default"])
                gauge("foo", tags=["server_tag:eu"])
                gauge("foo", tags=["server_tag:eu", "server_tag:primary"])
                ```
            3. tag_not_null - This only sets tags in the metric if the value is not null
          You can use the `count` type to perform aggregation for queries that return multiple rows with
          the same or no tags.
    Columns without a name are ignored. To skip a column, enter:
    ```
      - {}
    ```
3. tags (optional) - A list of tags to apply to each metric.
4. collection_interval (optional) - The frequency at which to collect the metrics.
    If collection_interval is not set, the query will be run every check run.
    If the collection interval is less than check collection interval, the query will be run every check
    run.
    If the collection interval is greater than check collection interval, the query will NOT BE RUN
    exactly at the collection interval.
    The query will be run at the next check run after the collection interval has passed.
5. metric_prefix (optional) - The prefix to apply to each metric.

example.query: SELECT foo, COUNT(*) FROM table.events GROUP BY foo

options.name: tags
options.description:
A list of tags to attach to every metric and service check emitted by this instance.

Learn more about tagging at https://docs.datadoghq.com/tagging

options.name: service
options.description:
Attach the tag `service:<SERVICE>` to every metric, event, and service check emitted by this integration.

Overrides any `service` defined in the `init_config` section.

options.name: min_collection_interval
options.description:
This changes the collection interval of the check. For more information, see:
https://docs.datadoghq.com/developers/write_agent_check/#collection-interval

options.name: empty_default_hostname
options.description:
This forces the check to send metrics with no hostname.

This is useful for cluster-level checks.

options.name: metric_patterns
options.description:
A mapping of metrics to include or exclude, with each entry being a regular expression.

Metrics defined in `exclude` will take precedence in case of overlap.
